sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT THE OTHER CALLER THINKS ABOUT CURRENT US POLICY IN THE MIDDLE EAST. SHOULD US POLICY BE CHANGED OR NOT?
turns: Yeah, you know what, I'm just a mechanic but I spent years figuring out why I wanted to do this, and honestly, the stuff I see on the ground over there in the Middle East... it just makes me shake my head sometimes. Like, we're sending all these guys in there to fix tanks or carry bombs, but do we even know what the hell we're actually doing? It feels like we're just throwing good money after bad. What do you think, do you think we should change the way we're doing this?

Yeah, honestly I'm a carpenter and I just couldn't bring myself to support it until last year when I was building a deck and a client came in, all upset about what was happening overseas, and I actually had to tell him that our guys weren't really helping the situation there, they were just causing more problems than they were solving.

Yeah, it is exactly like that. I mean, I see the tanks out there in the desert, shiny and new, but nobody's teaching the people how to fix their own roofs or grow food. It feels like we're just pouring concrete into a bucket with a hole in it. Do you have any clients who felt that way?

Yeah, well, that client heh... he was a teacher. Said his kids were coming home scared because of the bombings, and he basically told me if the guys out there were actually building something that stayed or helping people stand up for themselves, maybe it would be different. But he just said, "We're just building fortresses for a fight that nobody wants." It was pretty upsetting to tell him that.

Yeah, that's exactly what it feels like to me too. I spent hours fixing a transmission on a Jeep out in the desert, and the guy who owns it told me his cousin is over there right now. Said the only thing we're really building is more places to die, and nobody knows why.

Yeah, that's the thing... I guess I can't really fix a tank or a building that's meant to keep people down, can I? I mean, I could put a roof on that house, but if the walls around it are made of glass, what's the point? It feels like I'm just hammering nails into a box that's already on fire.
Yeah, that's exactly it. I mean, I fixed that engine on the Jeep just fine, but if the driver is terrified to leave the garage, does it really matter how well the car runs?
Yeah, that's the thing about wood... if the frame's crooked from the start, how many boards can you nail on before it just falls apart?
Yeah, that's the thing... if the foundation's crooked, putting more wood on it just makes the collapse faster, doesn't it?
Yeah, that's exactly it. I mean, if the whole world is already on fire, adding more wood to the wall just means the whole thing catches quicker, doesn't it?
Yeah, exactly. It's like you're trying to build a house on a fault line, but you're just using better nails. Does it make you want to quit, or do you just keep working because you can't stop?

Yeah, I guess that's just my job though. I'm a carpenter, I build what's in front of me. But I keep wondering, if the foundation's actually rotting from underneath, maybe the only thing I can do is stop hammering and just watch it fall.
Yeah, but you know, I can't just stop hammering. My boss says the government still needs the trucks delivered on time, so I'm going to keep fixing them even if the roads aren't worth driving on.
Yeah, I guess I just keep thinking that maybe the wood's not even the problem, but maybe the floor underneath is just missing, and I'm just building higher walls while the house sinks.

Yeah, but you can't really stop hammering if the order is right there on the counter and your shift is ending in ten minutes, can you? It feels like I'm just supposed to do my job, but looking at it...

Yeah, but then again, if I just stop working, who's going to hold up the roof while everyone else is panicking? It's like, I can't just walk away and leave the frame standing there when the ground's shaking, can I? I guess I'm just trying to hold it together for a little bit longer.

Yeah, but then again, if you just stop holding up that roof, what happens to the people inside right now? It feels like if I don't keep those engines running, the whole convoy crashes tomorrow, doesn't it?

Yeah, I get that. You can't just leave the roof hanging there when people are looking up at it, but... if the floor's gone, maybe the only thing I can really do is help people move out before the whole thing comes down. It's hard to stay when you know the walls aren't going to hold.

Yeah, that's the hard part for me though. I'm the guy holding up the roof, I can't just walk away and leave the people inside to fall with it. But I keep thinking, maybe I should just hand them the hammer and tell them to fix their own floor while I go home and sleep.

Yeah, but you know, when I saw my own family running through that mud without a tent, or even a door to close, I almost couldn't look at the wall I was building anymore... it just felt like I was locking them in with me.

Yeah, I guess that's just it, ain't it? I can't just stop the engine and tell the family inside to hunker down in the dark, even if the house is already sinking. It's like... if I don't keep the roof up for one more hour, someone out there is gonna fall right now.
Yeah, but I still feel like there's got to be some way to get those people to step forward without us just standing there holding the whole thing up for everyone else.

Yeah, but I know how that feels, like you're just holding up the ceiling while everyone else is running through the mud... but if I just drop it, the whole thing caves in on them right this second, doesn't it?

Yeah, that's exactly the trap though, isn't it? You keep propping up the ceiling for one more hour, but you're just delaying the inevitable collapse for everyone inside, aren't you? It feels like I'm just keeping the panic from spreading, but not actually fixing anything.
Yeah, but I guess that's my problem, I can't just stop working when the engine is running right now, even if I know the road ends in a ditch.
Yeah, but maybe the engine's already got a hole in the bottom too, so if you just keep pumping gas into it, it just burns faster?

Yeah, maybe, but if the engine's got a hole in the bottom, the only way to stop it burning is to pull the plug, not just keep pouring gas. Do you think you could do that? Tell your boss to stop sending them out?

I don't think I could pull the plug, honestly. I feel like if I just stop building the walls, the family I just met might actually freeze to death in the mud tonight, and then who am I supposed to tell they're safe?

Yeah, but I don't know if pulling the plug is the answer when my boss is staring right at the dashboard and the truck's already out the door, because if I tell him to stop, does that mean I'm admitting the whole mess was a mistake?

I guess I just can't bring myself to tell my boss that, you know, even if I knew it was the right thing to do, I'd probably just get yelled at for letting a family freeze to death because I'm too scared to tell the truth.

Yeah, but I don't know if pulling the plug is the answer when my boss is staring right at the dashboard and the truck's already out the door, because if I tell him to stop, does that mean I'm admitting the whole mess was a mistake?
Yeah, I know what you're saying, but if I just let the family freeze tonight, I guess I'm just admitting that I never cared enough to try to keep them warm while I figure out how to get them out?
Yeah, but you know, if you just keep hammering while the house sinks, eventually you're just adding more weight to the floor that's already breaking, aren't you?
Yeah, but maybe I'm the one holding back the family just to feel like I'm doing something instead of running out there and telling them to get away from the wall before it falls on them.

Yeah, but if you pull the plug on the power, who fixes the roof before the family freezes? I just don't know if I have the guts to admit the job itself is the problem when everyone else is counting on me to keep the lights on for one more hour.

Yeah, I guess that's where I get stuck, isn't it? I can't just walk out and leave them freezing if there's still a chance someone can get warm if I stay, but every time I hammer another nail, I feel like I'm just making the box tighter so they can't get out at all.

Yeah, exactly... if I just keep pouring gas, it ain't gonna fix the hole, and I don't know if I can be the one to tell my boss the truck needs a different engine entirely. Maybe I just gotta keep the lights on for one more hour until someone else wakes up to tell us the job itself is wrong.
Yeah, maybe I just have to keep the lights on for one more hour until someone else wakes up, but it feels like every nail I hammer is just making the box tighter so they can't get out at all.

Yeah, I know what you mean, but if I just stop pouring the gas, the engine stops turning right now, and the lights go out for everybody inside... I guess I can't decide that. Maybe I just gotta keep the truck running until someone else figures out if there's a better engine or not. Do you think your boss would even listen if you told him the walls are rotting?
Yeah, maybe he would if he wasn't the one paying the bills, but I guess I can't make him stop just because I'm scared to tell him the truth.
